title: SP638 bounded hairpin corridor cut/fill proof
hypothesis: A bounded ~700 m maximum-curvature SP638 slice using Unreal editor spline raise/lower deformation plus a separate neutral road/shoulder proof surface will remove road-ground clipping and materially improve rider-height readability without rebuilding the full Passo Giau terrain.
technical: Attempt 1 (run 36414967154) reached Unreal but did not execute the intended deformation: the edit layer name 'None' was invalid and the Python material setter name was wrong. Workspace cleanup and failure evidence upload passed.
The proof reused the persisted L_PassoGiauTerrainSpike.umap and did not redownload the 33 Veneto DTM tiles or rebuild the full Landscape.
Selected official-SP638 hairpin: s=15525 m on the 19.198 km source road; bounded slice length 685.369 m.
LandscapeProxy.editor_apply_spline ran on edit layer 'Layer' with 5.2 m core width, 16 m side falloff, 240 subdivisions, and both raise/lower enabled.
The transient proof generated 138 road segments and 138 shoulder/roadbed segments, captured 3840 x 2160, and passed the non-persistent mutation guard.
visual: Human/model visual review of the GREEN 3840 x 2160 proof rejects this candidate.
Positive: the road is now immediately readable as a road and no longer disappears into the Landscape in the camera foreground.
Reject: the camera-close uphill terrain still exposes severe vertical ribbing/terracing and block-like heightfield structure.
Reject: the neutral 10 m proof shoulder/roadbed reads as an oversized wedge/slab and creates implausible geometry around the hairpin.
Reject: the road/corridor transition is not yet a believable Alpine cut/embankment.
keep: Official Veneto SP638 centerline and persisted spline.
Fast proof path that reuses the persisted LFS map instead of rebuilding the full terrain.
LandscapeProxy.editor_apply_spline as a useful road-bed deformation primitive.
reject: Spline raise/lower plus a simple box-strip roadbed as the complete foreground terrain solution.
The 10 m uniform shoulder/roadbed strip used in this proof.
Using the macro Landscape itself for camera-close cliff/cut faces.
Global Landscape-resolution increases as the next response.
Asset dressing before the local cut/cliff/embankment geometry is credible.
learnings: The spline deformation technique materially improves road readability but does not solve the heightfield representation failure on steep rider-visible terrain.
The next improvement must replace the camera-close uphill/downhill corridor with dedicated local geometry rather than asking the macro Landscape to represent cliffs.
The experiment validates the fast bounded iteration loop: a new geometry technique can now be judged on one hairpin without a full 8 km x 8 km authoring pass.
A technically GREEN proof can and did fail the human visual gate.
next: R4.1B.3: generate a dedicated high-detail local ground/cut/embankment mesh for the same 685 m hairpin while retaining Landscape only as macro background.
Use Landscape Patch or a bounded Landscape deformation only to hide/intersect the macro terrain beneath that local mesh.
Replace the uniform shoulder slab with a cross-section-driven roadbed: asphalt, narrow shoulder, uphill cut, downhill embankment.
Render the same rider camera before adding vegetation, rocks or production materials.

attempts.note: Invalid edit layer name 'None' and nonexistent editor_set_landscape_material Python wrapper; intended cut/fill proof was not executed.
End-to-end 4K bounded proof passed technically; rider-camera result still fails foreground terrain/corridor quality.
